purposes.label: Paying a government agency or fine

context_chips.label: On the phone during the transaction
Mentions urgency, secrecy, or being told what to say
Cash withdrawal above the branch threshold

questions.why: A neutral opener. Every customer gets this one.

questions.text: Who's doing the work? I might know them.
questions.why: A real job has a named contractor. A cover story usually doesn't.

questions.text: Do you have a written estimate from them?
questions.why: Real contract work normally comes with paperwork the customer can describe.

questions.text: Tell me about the account it's going to. Whose name is it in, and which bank?
questions.why: Moving money between your own accounts has details a 'safe account' story lacks.

questions.text: Has anyone asked you to keep this between you and them?
questions.why: Scammers warn victims the bank will try to stop them.

questions.text: Would a cashier's check made out to them work instead? It's safer than carrying cash.
questions.why: Legitimate payees take checks. Refusing one without a reason is a coaching signature.

signals.label: On the phone during the visit
signals.rationale: Scammers often stay on the line to coach the customer through the withdrawal.

signals.label: Someone else directing them
signals.rationale: Another person steering the transaction can mean the customer isn't acting freely.

signals.label: Insists on cash
signals.rationale: Scams favour cash because it can't be traced or reversed.

signals.label: Seems rushed
signals.rationale: Urgency is a pressure tactic, though it's common in ordinary errands too.

signals.label: Mentioned urgency or secrecy
signals.rationale: Being told to hurry or keep quiet is a hallmark of coaching.

signals.label: Unusual for this customer
signals.rationale: The teller's knowledge of the customer is a real but weak signal.

signals.label: Answer relayed by caller
signals.rationale: The customer repeated what someone on the phone told them to say.

signals.label: Told not to discuss with the bank
signals.rationale: Scammers warn victims the bank will try to stop them. Being told to keep it quiet is one of the strongest single indicators.

signals.label: Missing details
signals.rationale: A plausible purpose with none of the details a real one would have.

signals.label: Story changed
signals.rationale: Answers that shift between questions suggest a rehearsed story under strain.

signals.label: Turned down a safer option
signals.rationale: Legitimate payees take checks. Refusing one without a reason is a coaching signature.

signals.label: Clear purpose
signals.rationale: The customer described the purpose in their own specific terms.

signals.label: Named the payee
signals.rationale: A real job or purchase has a named person or business behind it.

signals.label: Written estimate exists
signals.rationale: A real contract job normally has paperwork the customer can describe.

signals.label: Account in their own name
signals.rationale: Money moving between the customer's own accounts at a bank they chose.

signals.label: Accepted a cashier's check
signals.rationale: Willingness to use a traceable payment is strong evidence the payee is real.
